verses.1:1: Paul, a servant of Christ Jesus, called as an apostle, separated for the gospel of God,
verses.1:2: which He promised beforehand through His prophets in the sacred Scriptures,
verses.1:3: concerning His Son, who came from the seed of David according to the flesh,
verses.1:4: and was appointed Son of God in power according to the Spirit of holiness by the resurrection of the dead, Jesus Christ our Lord,
verses.1:5: through whom we received grace and apostleship for the obedience of faith among all the nations on behalf of His name,
verses.1:6: among whom you also are those who are called of Jesus Christ,
verses.1:7: to all who are in Rome, beloved by God, called as saints: Grace be to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.1:8: First, I give thanks to my God through Jesus Christ concerning all of you, because your faith is proclaimed throughout the whole world.
verses.1:9: For God is my witness, whom I serve in my spirit in the gospel of His Son, how unceasingly I make mention of you,
verses.1:10: always in my prayers, pleading that somehow now at last I may be granted a way in the will of God to come to you.
verses.1:11: For I deeply long to see you, so that I may impart to you some spiritual gift in order that you may be firmly established—
verses.1:12: that is, to be comforted together among you through each other's faith, both yours and mine.
verses.1:13: Now I do not wish you to be ignorant, brethren, that many times I purposed to come to you—and was hindered until now—that I might obtain some fruit among you also, just as among the rest of the Gentiles.
verses.1:14: Both to Greeks and to barbarians, both to the wise and to the foolish, I am a debtor.
verses.1:15: Thus, as far as it depends on me, I am eager to proclaim the gospel also to you who are in Rome.
verses.1:16: For I am not ashamed of the gospel, for it is God's power for salvation to everyone who believes, first to the Jew and also to the Greek.
verses.1:17: For in it God's righteousness is revealed from faith to faith, even as it is written, "The righteous one shall live by faith."
verses.1:18: For the wrath of God is being revealed from heaven against all impiety and unrighteousness of men who suppress the truth in unrighteousness,
verses.1:19: because what may be known of God is manifest among them, for God has made it manifest to them.
verses.1:20: For His invisible realities, from the creation of the world, are clearly seen, being understood through the things that have been made—both His everlasting power and His divine nature—so that they are without excuse;
verses.1:21: because, though knowing God, they neither glorified Him as God nor gave Him thanks, but became vain in their reasonings, and their senseless heart was darkened.
verses.1:22: Declaring themselves to be wise, they became fools,
verses.1:23: and exchanged the glory of the incorruptible God for a likeness of the image of corruptible man, and of birds, and of four-footed beasts, and of creeping things.
verses.1:24: Therefore God delivered them over in the lusts of their hearts to uncleanness, for their bodies to be dishonored among themselves—
verses.1:25: those who exchanged the truth of God for the lie, and revered and served the creation rather than the Creator, who is blessed throughout the ages. Amen.
verses.1:26: For this cause God delivered them over to dishonorable passions; for their females exchanged natural relations for that which is against nature,
verses.1:27: and likewise also the males, forsaking natural relations with the female, were inflamed in their craving for one another, males with males committing indecency, and receiving in themselves the recompense that was due for their error.
verses.1:28: And just as they did not approve of keeping God in their knowledge, God delivered them over to a reprobate mind, to do the things that are not fitting,
verses.1:29: being filled with all unrighteousness, wickedness, covetousness, malice; full of envy, murder, strife, guile, malignity; whisperers,
verses.1:30: slanderers, haters of God, insolent, proud, boasters, devisers of evil, disobedient to parents,
verses.1:31: without understanding, faithless, without natural affection, unmerciful—
verses.1:32: who, knowing full well the righteous decree of God, that those who practice such things are worthy of death, not only do them, but also give hearty approval to those who practice them.
verses.2:1: Therefore you are without excuse, O man, everyone who judges; for in judging another you condemn yourself, because you who judge practice the very same things.
verses.2:2: Now we know that God's judgment is in accordance with truth upon those who practice such things.
verses.2:3: And do you reckon this, O man—you who judge those who practice such things and yet do them—that you yourself will escape the judgment of God?
verses.2:4: Or do you despise the riches of His kindness and His forbearance and His longsuffering, not recognizing that God's kindness leads you to repentance?
verses.2:5: But according to your stubbornness and impenitent heart, you are storing up for yourself wrath in the day of wrath and of the revelation of God's righteous judgment,
verses.2:6: who will render to each according to his works:
verses.2:7: to those who by perseverance in good work seek glory, honor, and incorruption, eternal life;
verses.2:8: but to those who act from selfish ambition and disobey the truth, yet obey unrighteousness—wrath and indignation,
verses.2:9: tribulation and distress upon every soul of man who works evil, of the Jew first and also of the Greek;
verses.2:10: but glory and honor and peace to everyone who works what is good, to the Jew first and also to the Greek.
verses.2:11: For with God there is no partiality.
verses.2:12: For all who have sinned apart from the law shall also perish apart from the law, and all who have sinned within the law shall be judged by the law.
verses.2:13: For the hearers of the law are not righteous before God, but the doers of the law will be justified.
verses.2:14: For whenever Gentiles, who do not possess the law, do by nature the things of the law, these, though not having the law, are a law to themselves;
verses.2:15: for they demonstrate the work of the law written on their hearts, their conscience bearing witness alongside, and their thoughts among themselves accusing or else defending them,
verses.2:16: on the day when God judges the hidden things of men, according to my gospel, through Christ Jesus.
verses.2:17: But if you bear the name of Jew, and rest upon the law, and boast in God,
verses.2:18: and know His will, and approve what is superior, being instructed from the law,
verses.2:19: and are persuaded that you yourself are a guide of the blind, a light to those in darkness,
verses.2:20: a corrector of the foolish, a teacher of babes, possessing the form of knowledge and of the truth in the law—
verses.2:21: you, then, who teach another, do you not teach yourself? You who proclaim not to steal, do you steal?
verses.2:22: You who say not to commit adultery, do you commit adultery? You who detest idols, do you plunder temples?
verses.2:23: You who boast in the law, do you dishonor God by the transgression of the law?
verses.2:24: For "because of you the name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles," even as it is written.
verses.2:25: For circumcision indeed is of benefit if you practice the law; but if you are a transgressor of the law, your circumcision has become uncircumcision.
verses.2:26: Therefore, if the uncircumcised man keeps the righteous ordinances of the law, will not his uncircumcision be reckoned as circumcision?
verses.2:27: And he who is uncircumcised by nature, fulfilling the law, shall judge you who, with the letter and circumcision, are a transgressor of the law.
verses.2:28: For he is not a Jew who is so outwardly, nor is that circumcision which is outward in the flesh;
verses.2:29: but he is a Jew who is so inwardly, and circumcision is of the heart, by the Spirit, not by the letter; whose praise is not from men, but from God.
verses.3:1: What advantage, then, belongs to the Jew, or what is the benefit of circumcision?
verses.3:2: Much in every way. First of all, because the oracles of God were entrusted to them.
verses.3:3: For what if some were unfaithful? Will their unfaithfulness make void the faithfulness of God?
verses.3:4: May it never be! Rather, let God prove true, and every man a liar, just as it is written: "That You may be justified in Your words, and shall prevail when You are judged."
verses.3:5: But if our unrighteousness confirms the righteousness of God, what shall we say? Is God unrighteous who inflicts wrath? I speak in human terms.
verses.3:6: May it never be! For otherwise, how shall God judge the world?
verses.3:7: Yet if through my falsehood the truth of God has abounded to His glory, why am I also still judged as a sinner?
verses.3:8: And why not say—as we are slandered and as some assert that we say—"Let us do evil that good may come"? Their judgment is just.
verses.3:9: What then? Are we at any advantage? Not at all; for we have already charged both Jews and Greeks that all are under sin,
verses.3:10: just as it is written: "There is none who is righteous, not even one;
verses.3:11: there is none who understands, there is none who seeks out God.
verses.3:12: All have turned aside; together they have become worthless; there is none who does goodness, not so much as one.
verses.3:13: Their throat is an open grave; with their tongues they have dealt deceitfully; the venom of asps is beneath their lips;
verses.3:14: whose mouth is filled with cursing and bitterness.
verses.3:15: Their feet are swift to shed blood;
verses.3:16: ruin and wretchedness are in their paths,
verses.3:17: and they have not known the way of peace.
verses.3:18: No fear of God is before their eyes."
verses.3:19: Now we know that whatever the law says, it speaks to those who are under the law, so that every mouth may be silenced and the whole world may become accountable to God.
verses.3:20: Because by works of the law no flesh shall be justified before Him; for through the law comes the knowledge of sin.
verses.3:21: But now, apart from the law, the righteousness of God has been manifested, attested by the Law and the Prophets—
verses.3:22: even the righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ, for all who believe; for there is no distinction.
verses.3:23: For all sinned and fall short of the glory of God,
verses.3:24: being justified as a free gift by His grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus,
verses.3:25: whom God put forward as a propitiation through faith in His blood, for a demonstration of His righteousness, because of the passing over of the sins committed beforehand
verses.3:26: in the forbearance of God, for the demonstration of His righteousness at the present time, so that He may be both just and the One who justifies the one who has faith in Jesus.
verses.3:27: Where, then, is boasting? It has been shut out. By what kind of law? That of works? No, but by a law of faith.
verses.3:28: For we reckon that a man is justified by faith apart from works of the law.
verses.3:29: Or is God the God of Jews alone? Is He not of Gentiles also? Yes, of Gentiles also,
verses.3:30: since indeed God is one, who shall justify the circumcised by faith and the uncircumcised through faith.
verses.3:31: Do we then nullify the law through faith? May it never be! Rather, we uphold the law.
verses.4:1: What then shall we say that Abraham, our forefather according to the flesh, has found?
verses.4:2: For if Abraham was justified by works, he has a ground for boasting, yet not before God.
verses.4:3: For what does the Scripture say? "Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness."
verses.4:4: Now to the one who works, the wage is not reckoned according to grace, but as a debt;
verses.4:5: but to the one who does not work, yet believes in Him who justifies the ungodly, his faith is reckoned as righteousness,
verses.4:6: just as David also speaks of the blessedness of the man to whom God reckons righteousness apart from works:
verses.4:7: "Blessed are they whose iniquities have been forgiven, and whose sins have been covered;
verses.4:8: blessed is the man to whom the Lord shall by no means reckon sin."
verses.4:9: Is this blessing then upon the circumcised, or upon the uncircumcised also? For we say, "Faith was reckoned to Abraham as righteousness."
verses.4:10: How then was it reckoned? While he was in circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision.
verses.4:11: And he received the sign of circumcision as a seal of the righteousness of the faith he had while uncircumcised, so that he might be the father of all who believe without being circumcised, that righteousness might be reckoned to them,
verses.4:12: and the father of the circumcised—for those who are not merely of the circumcision, but who also walk in the footsteps of the faith which our father Abraham had while in uncircumcision.
verses.4:13: For the promise to Abraham or to his seed, that he should be heir of the world, was not through the law, but through the righteousness of faith.
verses.4:14: For if those who are of the law are heirs, faith has been rendered empty and the promise has been nullified;
verses.4:15: for the law produces wrath; yet where there is no law, neither is there transgression.
verses.4:16: For this reason it is by faith, that it might be according to grace, so that the promise may be guaranteed to all the seed—not only to those who are of the law, but also to those who are of the faith of Abraham, who is the father of us all
verses.4:17: (just as it is written: "I have appointed you a father of many nations") before God, in whom he believed—the One who gives life to the dead and calls the things that are not as though they were;
verses.4:18: who, beyond hope, believed in hope, that he might become a father of many nations, according to what had been spoken: "So shall your seed be."
verses.4:19: And without growing weak in faith, he considered his own body, now already dead—being about a hundred years old—as well as the deadness of Sarah's womb;
verses.4:20: yet toward the promise of God he did not waver through unbelief, but grew strong in faith, giving glory to God,
verses.4:21: and being fully assured that what He had promised, He was also able to do.
verses.4:22: Therefore also it was reckoned to him as righteousness.
verses.4:23: Now it was not written on his account alone that it was reckoned to him,
verses.4:24: but on our account also, to whom it is to be reckoned—those who believe in Him who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead,
verses.4:25: who was delivered over on account of our trespasses and was raised on account of our justification.
verses.5:1: Having been justified, therefore, by faith, let us have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ,
verses.5:2: through whom also we have gained access by faith into this grace in which we stand, and we exult in the hope of the glory of God.
verses.5:3: And not only so, but we also exult in tribulations, knowing that tribulation works steadfastness,
verses.5:4: and steadfastness, tested character; and tested character, hope.
verses.5:5: And hope does not put to shame, for the love of God has been poured forth in our hearts through the Holy Spirit who was given to us.
verses.5:6: For even while we were still weak, at the appointed time Christ died for the ungodly.
verses.5:7: For scarcely will one die for a righteous man; yet perhaps for the good man someone might even dare to die.
verses.5:8: But God shows forth His own love toward us, in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.
verses.5:9: Much more, therefore, having now been justified by His blood, we shall be saved through Him from the wrath.
verses.5:10: For if, while being enemies, we were reconciled to God through the death of His Son, much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by His life.
verses.5:11: And not only so, but we also exult in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now received the reconciliation.
verses.5:12: Therefore, even as through one man sin entered into the world, and death through sin, so also death passed through to all men, because all sinned—
verses.5:13: for until the law, sin was in the world, yet sin is not reckoned when there is no law.
verses.5:14: Yet death reigned from Adam to Moses, even over those who did not sin in the likeness of Adam's transgression, who is a type of the One who was to come.
verses.5:15: But not as the trespass, so also is the gracious gift. For if by the trespass of the one the many died, much more did the grace of God and the gift in the grace of the one man Jesus Christ abound to the many.
verses.5:16: And not as through the one who sinned is the gift; for the judgment came from one to condemnation, but the gracious gift came from many trespasses to justification.
verses.5:17: For if by the trespass of the one death reigned through the one, much more shall those who receive the abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness reign in life through the One, Jesus Christ.
verses.5:18: Therefore, even as through one trespass it resulted in condemnation for all men, so also through one act of righteousness it resulted in justification of life for all men.
verses.5:19: For even as through the disobedience of the one man the many were constituted sinners, so also through the obedience of the One the many shall be constituted righteous.
verses.5:20: Now the law entered alongside, that the trespass might multiply; yet where sin multiplied, grace abounded far more,
verses.5:21: that just as sin reigned in death, so too might grace reign through righteousness to eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.
verses.6:1: What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, that grace may multiply?
verses.6:2: Far be it! We who died to sin, how shall we live in it any longer?
verses.6:3: Or are you unaware that all of us who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into His death?
verses.6:4: Therefore we were buried together with Him through baptism into death, so that even as Christ was raised from among the dead through the glory of the Father, so also we should walk in newness of life.
verses.6:5: For if we have been joined together in the likeness of His death, indeed we shall also be in that of His resurrection,
verses.6:6: knowing this, that our old man was crucified together with Him, in order that the body of sin might be brought to nothing, so that we should no longer be enslaved to sin.
verses.6:7: For the one who has died has been acquitted from sin.
verses.6:8: Now if we died together with Christ, we believe that we shall also live with Him,
verses.6:9: knowing that Christ, once raised from the dead, no longer dies; death exercises dominion over Him no more.
verses.6:10: For in that He died, He died to sin once for all; but in that He lives, He lives to God.
verses.6:11: In the same manner, you also must reckon yourselves to be dead to sin, yet alive to God in Christ Jesus.
verses.6:12: Therefore do not let sin reign in your mortal body, so as to obey its desires,
verses.6:13: nor present your members to sin as weapons of unrighteousness, but present yourselves to God as those alive from the dead, and your members to God as weapons of righteousness.
verses.6:14: For sin shall not be master over you, because you are not under law, but under grace.
verses.6:15: What then? Shall we sin because we are not under law, but under grace? Far be it!
verses.6:16: Do you not know that to whomever you offer yourselves as slaves for obedience, you are slaves to the one whom you obey, either of sin to death, or of obedience to righteousness?
verses.6:17: But thanks be to God that, though you were slaves of sin, you obeyed from the heart that pattern of teaching to which you were delivered,
verses.6:18: and having been freed from sin, you were made slaves to righteousness.
verses.6:19: I speak after the manner of men because of the weakness of your flesh. For even as you once offered your members as slaves to impurity and to lawlessness resulting in lawlessness, so now offer your members as slaves to righteousness resulting in sanctification.
verses.6:20: For when you were slaves of sin, you were free with respect to righteousness.
verses.6:21: What fruit, therefore, did you then have in those things of which you are now ashamed? Indeed, the end of those things is death.
verses.6:22: But now, having been freed from sin and made slaves to God, you have your fruit leading to sanctification, and the end, eternal life.
verses.6:23: For the wages of sin is death, yet the gracious gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.
verses.7:1: Or are you unaware, brethren—for I speak to those who know law—that the law rules over a man for as long as he lives?
verses.7:2: For a married woman is bound by law to her living husband; yet if the husband dies, she is released from the law concerning the husband.
verses.7:3: Therefore, while her husband is living, she shall be called an adulteress if she is joined to another man; yet if her husband dies, she is free from that law, so that she is not an adulteress when she is joined to another man.
verses.7:4: So then, my brethren, you also were put to death to the law through the body of Christ, so that you might be joined to another—to Him who was raised from the dead—in order that we might bear fruit to God.
verses.7:5: For when we were in the flesh, the passions of sins, brought about through the law, were working in our members to bear fruit to death.
verses.7:6: Yet now we have been released from the law, having died to that in which we were held captive, so that we serve in newness of the Spirit and not in oldness of the letter.
verses.7:7: What shall we say then? Is the law sin? Far be it! Rather, I would not have come to know sin except through the law; indeed, I would not have known coveting had the law not said, "You shall not covet."
verses.7:8: Yet sin, taking opportunity through the commandment, produced in me every covetous desire; for apart from law, sin is dead.
verses.7:9: Once I was alive apart from law; yet when the commandment came, sin sprang to life,
verses.7:10: and I died; and the commandment which was for life was found in my case to result in death.
verses.7:11: For sin, seizing opportunity through the commandment, deceived me, and through it slew me.
verses.7:12: Thus the law indeed is holy, and the commandment is holy, righteous, and good.
verses.7:13: Did that which is good, then, become death to me? Far be it! Rather, it was sin, that it might be shown to be sin, working death in me through what is good, so that through the commandment sin might become sinful beyond measure.
verses.7:14: For we know that the law is spiritual, yet I am of flesh, sold under sin.
verses.7:15: For what I perform, I do not understand; for it is not what I desire that I practice, but what I hate, that I do.
verses.7:16: Now if I do what I do not desire, I concur with the law that it is good.
verses.7:17: As it is, then, it is no longer I who perform it, but sin dwelling within me.
verses.7:18: For I know that in me—that is, in my flesh—no good thing dwells; for the will to do it is present with me, yet the performing of what is good is not.
verses.7:19: For I do not do the good that I desire, rather the evil that I do not desire, this I practice.
verses.7:20: Now if I do that which I do not desire, it is no longer I who perform it, but sin dwelling within me.
verses.7:21: I find therefore this law, that when I desire to do what is good, evil is right at hand with me.
verses.7:22: For I take delight in the law of God in my inner man,
verses.7:23: yet I behold another law in my members, waging war against the law of my mind and leading me captive into the law of sin which is in my members.
verses.7:24: What a wretched man I am! Who shall deliver me from the body of this death?
verses.7:25: Thanks be to God through Jesus Christ our Lord! Accordingly, I myself serve the law of God with the mind, yet with the flesh the law of sin.
verses.8:1: Now therefore there is no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus;
verses.8:2: for the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus has set you free from the law of sin and of death.
verses.8:3: For what was impossible to the law, in that it was weak through the flesh, God—having sent His own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh and concerning sin—condemned sin in the flesh,
verses.8:4: that the righteous requirement of the law might be fulfilled in us, who do not walk according to the flesh, but according to the Spirit.
verses.8:5: For those who live according to the flesh set their minds on the things of the flesh, but those who live according to the Spirit, the things of the Spirit.
verses.8:6: For the mind of the flesh is death, but the mind of the Spirit is life and peace;
verses.8:7: because the mind of the flesh is enmity toward God, for to the law of God it is not subject, nor indeed can it be;
verses.8:8: and those who are in the flesh cannot please God.
verses.8:9: Yet you are not in the flesh, but in the Spirit, if indeed the Spirit of God dwells in you. Now if anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, this one is not His.
verses.8:10: And if Christ is in you, the body indeed is dead because of sin, yet the spirit is life because of righteousness.
verses.8:11: And if the Spirit of Him who raised up Jesus from the dead dwells in you, He who raised Christ Jesus from the dead shall give life also to your mortal bodies through His Spirit who dwells in you.
verses.8:12: Therefore, brethren, we are debtors, not to the flesh, to live according to the flesh;
verses.8:13: for if you live according to the flesh, you are about to die, but if by the Spirit you put to death the deeds of the body, you shall live.
verses.8:14: For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, these are sons of God.
verses.8:15: For you did not receive a spirit of bondage again to fear, but you received the Spirit of adoption as sons, by whom we cry, "Abba, Father!"
verses.8:16: The Spirit Himself bears witness together with our spirit that we are children of God;
verses.8:17: and if children, also heirs: heirs indeed of God, and joint heirs with Christ, if indeed we suffer together with Him, that we may also be glorified together with Him.
verses.8:18: For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory that is about to be revealed to us.
verses.8:19: For the earnest expectation of the creation eagerly awaits the revealing of the sons of God;
verses.8:20: for the creation was subjected to vanity, not willingly, but on account of Him who subjected it, in hope
verses.8:21: that the creation itself also shall be set free from the bondage of corruption into the liberty of the glory of the children of God.
verses.8:22: For we know that the whole creation groans together and travails in birth pangs together until now;
verses.8:23: and not only so, but we ourselves also, having the firstfruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, eagerly awaiting adoption as sons, the redemption of our body.
verses.8:24: For in hope we were saved; yet hope that is seen is not hope, for what a man sees, why does he still hope for it?
verses.8:25: But if we hope for that which we do not see, through steadfast endurance we eagerly await it.
verses.8:26: And in like manner the Spirit also helps our weakness; for what we should pray as we ought we do not know, but the Spirit Himself makes intercession with groanings unutterable,
verses.8:27: and He who searches the hearts knows what is the mind of the Spirit, because according to God He makes intercession on behalf of the saints.
verses.8:28: Now we know that for those who love God, all things work in concert for good—for those who are called according to His purpose.
verses.8:29: For whom He foreknew, He also predestined to be conformed to the image of His Son, that He might be the firstborn among many brethren;
verses.8:30: and whom He predestined, these He also called; and whom He called, these He also justified; and whom He justified, these He also glorified.
verses.8:31: What then shall we say to these things? If God is for us, who is against us?
verses.8:32: He indeed who did not spare His own Son, but delivered Him up on behalf of us all, how shall He not also with Him freely grant us all things?
verses.8:33: Who shall bring a charge against God's elect? It is God who justifies;
verses.8:34: who is he who condemns? It is Christ Jesus who died, yes rather, who was raised, who also is at the right hand of God, who also makes intercession on our behalf.
verses.8:35: Who shall part us from the love of Christ? Shall tribulation, or anguish, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword?
verses.8:36: Even as it is written, "For Your sake we are put to death all the day long; we were accounted as sheep for slaughter."
verses.8:37: Yet in all these things we prevail abundantly through Him who loved us.
verses.8:38: For I am persuaded that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor things present, nor things to come, nor powers,
verses.8:39: nor height, nor depth, nor any other created thing shall have power to part us from the love of God which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
verses.9:1: I speak the truth in Christ, I do not lie, my conscience bearing witness with me in the Holy Spirit,
verses.9:2: that I have great grief and unceasing anguish in my heart.
verses.9:3: For I could wish myself to be accursed from Christ on behalf of my brethren, my kinsmen according to the flesh,
verses.9:4: who are Israelites, to whom belong the adoption as sons, and the glory, and the covenants, and the giving of the law, and the sacred service, and the promises;
verses.9:5: whose are the fathers, and from whom comes the Christ according to the flesh—He who is over all, God blessed forevermore. Amen.
verses.9:6: Now it is not as though the word of God has failed; for not all those who are of Israel are Israel,
verses.9:7: neither, because they are the seed of Abraham, are they all children; rather, "In Isaac shall your seed be named."
verses.9:8: That is, the children of the flesh—these are not the children of God; rather, the children of the promise are reckoned as the seed.
verses.9:9: For this is a word of promise: "At this season I will come, and Sarah shall have a son."
verses.9:10: And not only so, but also when Rebekah had conceived by one man, our father Isaac—
verses.9:11: for while they were not yet born and had done nothing good or evil, so that the purpose of God according to election might abide,
verses.9:12: not from works, but from Him who calls—it was said to her, "The elder shall serve the younger,"
verses.9:13: just as it is written, "Jacob I loved, yet Esau I hated."
verses.9:14: What then shall we say? Is there unrighteousness with God? Far be it!
verses.9:15: For He says to Moses, "I will show mercy to whomever I show mercy, and I will show compassion to whomever I show compassion."
verses.9:16: Therefore it does not depend on him who wills, nor on him who runs, but on God who shows mercy.
verses.9:17: For the Scripture says to Pharaoh, "For this very reason I raised you up, that I might display My power in you, and that My name might be proclaimed in all the earth."
verses.9:18: Therefore, on whomever He wills He shows mercy, and whomever He wills He hardens.
verses.9:19: You will say to me then, "Why then does He still find fault? For who has withstood His will?"
verses.9:20: On the contrary, O man, who are you to answer back to God? Shall that which is molded say to him who molded it, "Why did you make me like this?"
verses.9:21: Or does the potter not have authority over the clay, from the same lump to fashion one vessel for honor and another for dishonor?
verses.9:22: What if God, desiring to display His wrath and make His power known, bore with much longsuffering vessels of wrath fitted for destruction,
verses.9:23: and in order that He might make known the riches of His glory upon vessels of mercy, which He prepared beforehand for glory—
verses.9:24: even us whom He also called, not from among the Jews only, but also from among the Gentiles?
verses.9:25: As He also says in Hosea: "I will call those who are not My people 'My people,' and her who was not loved 'Beloved.'"
verses.9:26: "And it shall be, in the place where it was spoken to them, 'You are not My people,' there they shall be called sons of the living God."
verses.9:27: And Isaiah cries out concerning Israel: "Though the number of the sons of Israel be as the sand of the sea, it is the remnant that shall be saved;
verses.9:28: for the Lord will execute His word upon the earth, finishing it and cutting it short."
verses.9:29: And just as Isaiah foretold: "Had the Lord of Sabaoth not left us a seed, we would have become as Sodom, and we would have been likened to Gomorrah."
verses.9:30: What then shall we say? That Gentiles, who were not pursuing righteousness, attained righteousness, even the righteousness that is by faith;
verses.9:31: yet Israel, pursuing a law of righteousness, did not attain to that law.
verses.9:32: Why? Because it was not by faith, but as if by works. They stumbled over the stone of stumbling,
verses.9:33: just as it is written: "Behold, I set in Zion a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense, and he who believes on Him shall not be put to shame."
verses.10:1: Brethren, my heart's desire and my supplication to God on their behalf is for their salvation.
verses.10:2: For I testify concerning them that they have a zeal for God, yet not according to true knowledge.
verses.10:3: For being ignorant of the righteousness of God, and seeking to establish their own, they did not submit themselves to the righteousness of God.
verses.10:4: For the end of the law is Christ, for righteousness to everyone who believes.
verses.10:5: For Moses writes concerning the righteousness that is by the law, "The man who does these things shall live by it."
verses.10:6: But the righteousness that is from faith speaks thus: "Do not say in your heart, 'Who shall ascend into heaven?'"—that is, to bring Christ down—
verses.10:7: or, "Who shall descend into the abyss?"—that is, to bring Christ up from the dead.
verses.10:8: Yet what does it say? "The word is near you, in your mouth and in your heart"—that is, the word of faith which we proclaim:
verses.10:9: that if you confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord, and believe in your heart that God raised Him from the dead, you shall be saved.
verses.10:10: For with the heart one believes for righteousness, and with the mouth confession is made for salvation.
verses.10:11: For the Scripture says, "Everyone who believes on Him shall not be put to shame."
verses.10:12: For there is no distinction between Jew and Greek; for the same Lord is Lord of all, abounding in riches toward all who call upon Him.
verses.10:13: For "everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord shall be saved."
verses.10:14: How then shall they call upon Him in whom they have not believed? And how shall they believe in Him whom they have not heard? And how shall they hear without one who proclaims?
verses.10:15: And how shall they proclaim unless they are sent? Just as it is written: "How beautiful are the feet of those who bring glad tidings of good things!"
verses.10:16: Yet not all obeyed the gospel; for Isaiah says, "Lord, who has believed our report?"
verses.10:17: Therefore faith comes by hearing, and hearing through the word of Christ.
verses.10:18: Yet I ask, have they not heard? Indeed they have: "Into all the earth has their voice gone forth, and to the ends of the world their words."
verses.10:19: Yet I ask, did Israel not know? First Moses declares: "I will stir you to jealousy by those who are not a nation; by a nation without understanding I will provoke you to anger."
verses.10:20: And Isaiah speaks boldly, saying: "I was found by those who did not seek Me; I showed Myself openly to those who did not inquire of Me."
verses.10:21: Yet concerning Israel he says: "All the day long I stretched forth My hands to a disobedient and defiant people."
verses.11:1: I say then, has God cast off His people? May it never be! For I myself am an Israelite, from the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.
verses.11:2: God has not cast off His people whom He foreknew. Or do you not know what the Scripture says concerning Elijah, how he pleads with God against Israel?
verses.11:3: "Lord, they have slain Your prophets, they have overthrown Your altars, and I alone have been left, and they are seeking my life."
verses.11:4: But what does the divine reply say to him? "I have kept for Myself seven thousand men who have not bent the knee to Baal."
verses.11:5: In the same way, then, at this present time also, there has come to be a remnant according to the election of grace.
verses.11:6: But if by grace, it is no longer by works; otherwise grace ceases to be grace.
verses.11:7: What then? That which Israel earnestly seeks, it did not obtain; yet the elect obtained it, while the rest were hardened,
verses.11:8: just as it is written: "God gave them a spirit of stupor, eyes not to see and ears not to hear, down to this present day."
verses.11:9: And David says: "May their table become a snare and a trap, and a stumbling block and a recompense to them;
verses.11:10: may their eyes be darkened so as not to see, and bow down their back continually."
verses.11:11: I say then, did they stumble so that they should fall? May it never be! Rather, by their transgression salvation has come to the Gentiles, to provoke them to jealousy.
verses.11:12: Now if their transgression is riches for the world, and their loss is riches for the Gentiles, how much more will their fullness be!
verses.11:13: Now I speak to you who are Gentiles: since, then, I am an apostle of the Gentiles, I magnify my ministry,
verses.11:14: if somehow I may provoke my own flesh to jealousy and save some from among them.
verses.11:15: For if their casting away brings reconciliation for the world, what will their reception be but life from the dead?
verses.11:16: And if the firstfruit is holy, so also is the lump; and if the root is holy, so also are the branches.
verses.11:17: Yet if some of the branches were broken off, and you, being a wild olive shoot, were grafted in among them and became a partaker of the root, of the richness of the olive tree,
verses.11:18: do not boast over the branches. But if you do boast—it is not you who bear the root, but the root bears you.
verses.11:19: Then you will say, "Branches were broken off in order that I might be grafted in."
verses.11:20: True enough! By unbelief they were broken off, whereas you stand firm by faith. Do not be high-minded, but fear;
verses.11:21: for if God did not spare the natural branches, He will not spare you either.
verses.11:22: Behold, then, the kindness and severity of God: toward those who fell, severity; but toward you, the kindness of God, if you abide in that kindness; otherwise you also will be cut off.
verses.11:23: And they too, if they do not remain in unbelief, will be grafted in; for God has power to graft them in again.
verses.11:24: For if you were cut from what is by nature a wild olive tree, and were grafted contrary to nature into a cultivated olive tree, how much more shall these, the natural branches, be grafted into their own olive tree!
verses.11:25: For I do not wish you to be unaware of this mystery, brethren, lest you be wise in your own estimation: a partial hardening has come upon Israel until the fullness of the Gentiles has entered in,
verses.11:26: and thus all Israel shall be saved, even as it is written: "Out of Zion shall come the Deliverer; He shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob.
verses.11:27: And this is the covenant from Me to them, when I take away their sins."
verses.11:28: With respect to the gospel, they are enemies for your sake; yet with respect to election, they are beloved because of the fathers.
verses.11:29: For the gracious gifts and the calling of God are never revoked.
verses.11:30: For just as you once disobeyed God, yet now have been shown mercy because of their disobedience,
verses.11:31: so these also have now disobeyed, in order that through the mercy shown to you they themselves may now be shown mercy.
verses.11:32: For God has shut up all in disobedience, so that He may show mercy to all.
verses.11:33: O the depth of the riches and wisdom and knowledge of God! How unsearchable His judgments, and how untraceable His ways!
verses.11:34: For who has understood the mind of the Lord, or who has served as His counselor?
verses.11:35: Or who has given beforehand to Him, so that it shall be repaid to him?
verses.11:36: For from Him and through Him and to Him are all things; to Him be the glory throughout all ages. Amen.
verses.12:1: I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the compassions of God, to present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, well-pleasing to God, which is your reasonable worship;
verses.12:2: and do not be conformed to this age, but be transformed by the renewing of the mind, that you may prove what is the will of God, that which is good and well-pleasing and perfect.
verses.12:3: For through the grace given to me I say to everyone who is among you not to think more highly than he ought to think, but to think with sober-mindedness, according as God has apportioned to each a measure of faith.
verses.12:4: For even as in one body we have many members, yet all the members do not have the same function,
verses.12:5: so we, being many, are one body in Christ, and individually members one of another.
verses.12:6: Now having differing gifts according to the grace given to us: whether prophecy, let us prophesy according to the proportion of faith;
verses.12:7: or ministry, in our ministering; or he who teaches, in his teaching;
verses.12:8: or he who exhorts, in his exhortation; he who imparts, in simplicity; he who leads, with diligence; he who shows mercy, with cheerfulness.
verses.12:9: Let love be without hypocrisy: abhorring that which is evil, cleaving to that which is good;
verses.12:10: in brotherly love tenderly affectionate one toward another; in honor outdoing one another;
verses.12:11: in diligence not slothful; in spirit fervent; serving the Lord;
verses.12:12: in hope rejoicing; in tribulation enduring; in prayer continuing steadfastly;
verses.12:13: sharing in the needs of the saints; pursuing hospitality.
verses.12:14: Bless those who persecute; bless, and do not curse.
verses.12:15: Rejoice with those who rejoice; weep with those who weep.
verses.12:16: Be of the same mind one toward another; not setting your mind on lofty things, but associating with the lowly. Do not become wise in your own estimation.
verses.12:17: Repaying no one evil for evil; taking thought for honorable things before all men;
verses.12:18: if it is possible, as much as depends on you, living at peace with all men;
verses.12:19: not avenging yourselves, beloved, but give place to wrath, for it is written, "To Me belongs vengeance; I will recompense, says the Lord."
verses.12:20: Rather, "If your enemy hungers, feed him; if he thirsts, give him a drink; for in doing this you shall heap coals of fire upon his head."
verses.12:21: Do not be conquered by evil, but conquer evil through good.
verses.13:1: Let every soul submit to the governing authorities; for no authority exists except by God, and those that exist have been ordained by God.
verses.13:2: Therefore whoever resists authority has opposed the ordinance of God, and those who oppose it shall receive judgment upon themselves.
verses.13:3: For rulers are not a terror to good conduct, but to evil conduct. Do you desire not to fear the authority? Practice what is good, and you will receive praise from it;
verses.13:4: for it is a servant of God for your good. But if you do evil, be afraid, for it does not bear the sword in vain; for it is a servant of God, an avenger to bring wrath upon the one who practices evil.
verses.13:5: Therefore it is necessary to be in subjection, not only on account of wrath, but also for the sake of conscience.
verses.13:6: For on this account you also pay taxes, since they are ministers of God, attending steadfastly to this very thing.
verses.13:7: Render to everyone what is due: taxes to whom taxes are due, revenue to whom revenue, fear to whom fear, honor to whom honor.
verses.13:8: Owe nothing to anyone, except to love one another; for whoever loves another has fulfilled the law.
verses.13:9: For these commandments—"You shall not commit adultery," "You shall not murder," "You shall not steal," "You shall not covet," and any other commandment there may be—are summed up in this word: "You shall love your neighbor as yourself."
verses.13:10: Love works no harm to a neighbor; thus love is the fulfillment of the law.
verses.13:11: And do this, discerning the time, that it is already the hour for you to awaken from sleep; for our salvation is nearer now than when we came to believe.
verses.13:12: The night is far advanced, and the day has drawn near. Let us therefore lay aside the works of darkness, and put on the armor of light.
verses.13:13: Let us walk honorably, as in the daytime, not in revelry and drunkenness, not in sexual immorality and licentiousness, not in strife and jealousy,
verses.13:14: but clothe yourselves with the Lord Jesus Christ, and do not make provision for the flesh to fulfill its lusts.
verses.14:1: Now receive the one who is weak in faith, not for debates over opinions.
verses.14:2: One has faith to eat all things, while the one who is weak eats vegetables.
verses.14:3: Do not let the one who eats despise the one who does not eat, and do not let the one who does not eat judge the one who eats, for God has received him.
verses.14:4: Who are you to judge the household servant of another? Before his own master he stands or falls; yet he shall be made to stand, for the Lord is able to make him stand.
verses.14:5: One regards one day above another, while another regards every day alike; let each person be fully persuaded in his own mind.
verses.14:6: The one who observes the day observes it to the Lord. And the one who eats eats to the Lord, for he gives thanks to God; and the one who does not eat, to the Lord he does not eat, and he gives thanks to God.
verses.14:7: For no one among us lives to himself, and no one dies to himself;
verses.14:8: for whether we live, we live to the Lord, or whether we die, we die to the Lord. Therefore, whether we live or whether we die, we belong to the Lord.
verses.14:9: For to this purpose Christ died and lived again, that He might be Lord over both the dead and the living.
verses.14:10: But you, why do you judge your brother? Or you also, why do you hold your brother in contempt? For we shall all stand before the judgment seat of God.
verses.14:11: For it is written: "As I live," says the Lord, "to Me every knee shall bow, and every tongue shall confess to God."
verses.14:12: Therefore, each one of us shall render an account concerning himself to God.
verses.14:13: Therefore let us no longer judge one another, but rather resolve this: not to place a stumbling block or a snare before a brother.
verses.14:14: I know and am persuaded in the Lord Jesus that nothing is unclean of itself; yet to the one who reckons anything to be unclean, to him it is unclean.
verses.14:15: For if because of food your brother is grieved, you are no longer walking according to love. Do not by your food destroy that one for whom Christ died.
verses.14:16: Therefore do not let your good be reviled.
verses.14:17: For the kingdom of God is not in food and drink, but in righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit;
verses.14:18: for the one who serves Christ in this way is well-pleasing to God and approved among men.
verses.14:19: So then let us pursue the things of peace and the things that build up one another.
verses.14:20: Do not for the sake of food tear down the work of God. All things indeed are clean, yet it is evil for the man who causes stumbling by his eating.
verses.14:21: It is good not to eat meat, nor to drink wine, nor to do anything by which your brother stumbles, or is ensnared, or becomes weak.
verses.14:22: The faith that you hold, keep to yourself before God. Blessed is the one who does not judge himself in what he approves;
verses.14:23: but the one who doubts stands condemned if he eats, because it is not from faith; and everything that is not from faith is sin.
verses.15:1: Now we who are strong ought to bear the infirmities of the weak, and not to please ourselves.
verses.15:2: Let each one of us please his neighbor for his good, to build him up.
verses.15:3: For Christ also did not please Himself, but as it is written: "The reproaches of those who cast reproach on You fell upon Me."
verses.15:4: For whatever was written beforehand was written for our teaching, that through steadfastness and through the consolation of the Scriptures we might have hope.
verses.15:5: Now may the God of steadfastness and consolation grant you to be of one mind among yourselves according to Christ Jesus,
verses.15:6: that with one accord and with one mouth you may glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.15:7: Therefore receive one another, even as Christ also received you, to the glory of God.
verses.15:8: For I tell you that Christ has become a servant to the circumcision on behalf of the truth of God, so as to confirm the promises given to the fathers,
verses.15:9: and in order that the Gentiles might glorify God for His mercy; as it is written: "Therefore I will praise You among the Gentiles, and to Your name I will sing praises."
verses.15:10: And again it says: "Be glad, O Gentiles, with His people."
verses.15:11: And again: "Praise the Lord, all you Gentiles, and let all the peoples extol Him."
verses.15:12: And again Isaiah says: "There shall be the Root of Jesse, even He who rises to rule over the Gentiles; on Him the Gentiles shall set their hope."
verses.15:13: Now may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace as you believe, so that you may abound in hope in the power of the Holy Spirit.
verses.15:14: Now I myself am persuaded regarding you, my brethren, that you yourselves are full of goodness, filled with all knowledge, and able to admonish one another as well.
verses.15:15: Nevertheless, on some points I have written to you rather boldly, by way of reminding you, because of the grace granted to me by God,
verses.15:16: to be a minister of Christ Jesus to the Gentiles, serving as a priest of the gospel of God, so that the offering of the Gentiles may become acceptable, sanctified by the Holy Spirit.
verses.15:17: Therefore in Christ Jesus I have cause for boasting in the things that pertain to God.
verses.15:18: For I will not venture to speak of anything except what Christ has accomplished through me for the obedience of the Gentiles, in word and deed,
verses.15:19: by the power of signs and wonders, by the power of the Spirit of God; so that from Jerusalem and around as far as Illyricum I have fully proclaimed the gospel of Christ,
verses.15:20: and thus making it my ambition to proclaim the gospel not where Christ was already named, lest I build upon another's foundation,
verses.15:21: but as it is written: "Those to whom no report was brought concerning Him shall see, and those who have not heard shall understand."
verses.15:22: Therefore I have also been hindered many times from coming to you.
verses.15:23: Yet now, having no longer any place in these regions, and having had a deep longing for many years to come to you,
verses.15:24: whenever I journey to Spain, for I hope to see you as I pass through and to be sent on my way there by you, once I have first had my fill in part of your company—
verses.15:25: yet now I am going to Jerusalem, ministering to the saints.
verses.15:26: For Macedonia and Achaia were well pleased to make a contribution for the poor among the saints in Jerusalem.
verses.15:27: Indeed they were well pleased, and they are debtors to them; for if the Gentiles have shared in their spiritual things, they are obligated also to serve them in material things.
verses.15:28: Therefore, when I have completed this and have sealed this fruit to them, I shall set out by way of you for Spain.
verses.15:29: And I know that in coming to you, I shall come in the fullness of the blessing of Christ.
verses.15:30: Now I appeal to you, brethren, through our Lord Jesus Christ and through the love of the Spirit, to strive together with me in prayers to God on my behalf,
verses.15:31: that I may be rescued from those who are disobedient in Judea, and that my ministry for Jerusalem may prove acceptable to the saints,
verses.15:32: so that in joy I may come to you through the will of God and find rest together with you.
verses.15:33: Now may the God of peace be with all of you. Amen.
verses.16:1: Now I commend to you our sister Phoebe, who is also a servant of the church that is in Cenchreae,
verses.16:2: that you may welcome her in the Lord in a manner worthy of the saints, and assist her in whatever matter she may have need of you; for indeed she herself has been a benefactor to many, and to myself as well.
verses.16:3: Greet Prisca and Aquila, my fellow workers in Christ Jesus,
verses.16:4: who ventured their own necks for my life, to whom not I alone give thanks, but also all the churches of the Gentiles;
verses.16:5: and greet the church that is in their house. Greet Epaenetus, my beloved, who is the firstfruits of Asia to Christ.
verses.16:6: Greet Mary, who labored greatly for you.
verses.16:7: Greet Andronicus and Junia, my kinsmen and my fellow prisoners, who are distinguished among the apostles, who were also in Christ before me.
verses.16:8: Greet Ampliatus, my beloved in the Lord.
verses.16:9: Greet Urbanus, our fellow worker in Christ, and Stachys, my beloved.
verses.16:10: Greet Apelles, who is approved in Christ. Greet those who belong to the household of Aristobulus.
verses.16:11: Greet Herodion, my kinsman. Greet those of the household of Narcissus who are in the Lord.
verses.16:12: Greet Tryphaena and Tryphosa, who labor in the Lord. Greet the beloved Persis, who labored greatly in the Lord.
verses.16:13: Greet Rufus, elect in the Lord, and his mother and mine.
verses.16:14: Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and the brethren who are with them.
verses.16:15: Greet Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas, and all the saints who are with them.
verses.16:16: Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the churches of Christ greet you.
verses.16:17: Now I exhort you, brethren, to take note of those who create divisions and stumbling blocks contrary to the teaching that you learned, and turn away from them;
verses.16:18: for such persons do not serve our Lord Christ, but their own belly, and through smooth speech and flattery they deceive the hearts of the unsuspecting.
verses.16:19: For your obedience has reached all. Therefore I rejoice over you; yet I desire you to be wise in what is good, and innocent in what is evil.
verses.16:20: And the God of peace will swiftly crush Satan beneath your feet. The grace of our Lord Jesus be with you.
verses.16:21: Timothy, my fellow worker, and Lucius, Jason, and Sosipater, my kinsmen, greet you.
verses.16:22: I, Tertius, who wrote this epistle, greet you in the Lord.
verses.16:23: Gaius, who is host to me and to the whole church, greets you. Erastus, the city treasurer, and our brother Quartus greet you.
verses.16:24: ⟦The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.⟧
verses.16:25: Now to Him who is able to strengthen you according to my gospel and the proclamation of Jesus Christ, according to the revelation of the mystery kept silent through ages eternal,
verses.16:26: but now made manifest, and through the prophetic Scriptures made known to all the nations, according to the command of the eternal God, for the obedience of faith—
verses.16:27: to the only wise God, through Jesus Christ, to whom be the glory forever. Amen.

notes.1:4: The Greek participle horisthentos may be rendered either 'appointed' (installed in messianic office) or 'declared' (publicly demonstrated). The phrase 'Spirit of holiness' reflects a Semitic idiom referring to the Holy Spirit.
notes.1:16: The Greek critical text reads simply 'the gospel,' omitting 'of Christ,' which appears in later manuscripts.
notes.1:17: Quoting Habakkuk 2:4, the Greek phrase 'by faith' (ek pisteos) may modify either 'shall live' ('The righteous one shall live by faith') or 'the righteous one' ('The one who is righteous by faith shall live').
notes.1:29: The Greek critical text lists four vices in the opening group, omitting 'sexual immorality' (porneia), and similarly lists four adjectives in verse 31 without 'unforgiving' (aspondous), both of which appear in later manuscripts.
notes.2:14: The Greek adverb 'by nature' (physei) can be construed either with the preceding clause ('who by nature do not possess the law') or with the following verb ('do by nature the things of the law').
notes.2:17: The Greek critical text reads 'But if' (Ei de), introducing a conditional clause that extends through verse 20, rather than 'Behold' or 'Indeed' (Ide) found in later manuscripts.
notes.2:27: Following the punctuation of the critical text, this verse stands as a declarative statement rather than a question; 'with the letter and circumcision' renders the Greek dia of attendant circumstance, denoting possession of the written law and circumcision.
notes.2:29: The Greek phrase 'en pneumati' can refer either to the Holy Spirit ('by the Spirit') or to the inner spiritual realm ('in spirit'). The mention of 'praise' also plays on the Hebrew meaning of the name Judah (Genesis 29:35).
notes.3:9: The Greek verb proechometha can be read as middle ("Are we at any advantage?") or passive ("Are we at a disadvantage?"); the theme of Jewish privilege from 3:1 favors the middle sense.
notes.3:22: The Greek phrase dia pisteos Iesou Christou is rendered "through faith in Jesus Christ" (objective genitive), though some understand it as "through the faithfulness of Jesus Christ" (subjective genitive). The critical Greek text reads "for all who believe" without the later expansion "and upon all."
notes.3:25: Greek hilasterion ("propitiation") is the Septuagint term for the mercy seat atop the ark of the covenant where atoning blood was sprinkled, expressing both atonement and the turning away of wrath.
notes.3:28: The critical Greek text reads gar ("For") rather than oun ("Therefore").
notes.4:1: The critical Greek text reads propatora ("forefather") rather than patera ("father"), and "according to the flesh" may modify either "our forefather" or "has found."
notes.4:19: The critical Greek text reads katenoesen ("he considered") without the negative ou ("did not consider") found in later manuscripts, showing that Abraham faced his physical condition squarely without weakening in faith.
notes.4:25: Both halves of the verse employ Greek dia with the accusative ("on account of"), pairing Christ's being delivered over with our trespasses and His resurrection with our justification.
notes.5:1: The earliest and strongest manuscripts read the hortatory subjunctive "let us have" (echomen), whereas later manuscripts read the indicative "we have" (echomen with omicron).
notes.5:6: The Greek critical text contains a double eti ("still/yet"), reflected here by "even while we were still weak."
notes.5:12: The phrase eph' ho is much debated, commonly understood as causal ("because"), though sometimes taken as consecutive ("with the result that") or relative ("in whom"). Paul breaks off his comparison here and resumes it in 5:18.
notes.6:5: The Greek term symphytoi literally means "grown together" or "organically united," conveying deep union with Christ.
notes.6:7: The verb dedikaiotai is the forensic term "has been justified" or "acquitted," indicating legal release from sin's claim through death.
notes.6:13: Greek hopla can mean either "instruments" or "weapons"; "weapons" highlights the military metaphor echoed in 6:23.
notes.6:23: Greek opsonia originally referred to a soldier's pay or rations, standing in sharp contrast to charisma, an unmerited gracious gift.
notes.7:6: The earliest manuscripts read the plural participle apothanontes ("having died" to that which held us), whereas later manuscripts read the singular apothanontos ("that being dead").
notes.7:21: Commentators debate whether ton nomon ("this law") refers to a general principle operating in the speaker or specifically to the Mosaic law.
notes.7:25: The Greek critical text reads charis to theo ("Thanks be to God"), whereas later manuscripts read eucharisto to theo ("I thank God").
notes.8:1: The Saints Greek Critical Text ends verse 1 at 'in Christ Jesus,' without the later explanatory clause found in some manuscripts.
notes.8:2: The Saints Greek Critical Text reads second-person singular se ('has set you free,' supported by Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, and early witnesses), whereas other manuscripts read first-person singular me ('me').
notes.8:15: Aramaic Abba ('Father') is preserved alongside the Greek ho pater, reflecting intimate filial address; huiothesia literally means 'adoption as sons.'
notes.8:28: Greek panta synergei eis agathon is rendered literally ('all things work together / in concert for good'); some manuscripts add ho theos ('God works all things together'), which is also a possible grammatical construal of the shorter text.
notes.8:38: The critical text places dynameis ('powers') after 'things present, nor things to come,' matching the earliest manuscripts.
notes.9:5: The Greek punctuation of the closing clause is debated; it may be read as a direct affirmation of Christ's deity ("who is over all, God blessed forevermore") or as a separate doxology addressed to God the Father ("May God, who is over all, be blessed forevermore").
notes.9:22: The Greek participle rendered "fitted" can be read as passive ("prepared by God") or middle ("having fitted themselves"), contrasting with the active verb "prepared beforehand" in 9:23.
notes.9:28: Following the earliest Greek witnesses, this text presents the concise form of Isaiah 10:22-23; later manuscripts expand the verse to align more closely with the fuller Septuagint wording.
notes.9:29: "Sabaoth" preserves the Greek transliteration of the Hebrew word for "hosts" or "armies," a Septuagint title designating God as ruler of the heavenly hosts.
notes.10:4: The Greek noun translated "end" (telos) encompasses both termination and goal or culmination, conveying that Christ both concludes the era of the Mosaic law and fulfills its intended purpose.
notes.10:5: The earliest Greek text reads the feminine singular "by it," referring back to the righteousness from the law, whereas later manuscripts read the plural "by them," referring to the commandments of Leviticus 18:5.
notes.10:15: Following the earliest Greek manuscripts, this quotation from Isaiah 52:7 omits the phrase "of those who proclaim the good news of peace" present in later textual witnesses.
notes.10:17: The critical Greek text reads "the word of Christ," whereas later manuscripts read "the word of God."
notes.11:4: The Greek places the feminine article before Baal, reflecting the Septuagint convention of substituting the feminine noun for shame (aischyne) when reading the pagan deity's name aloud.
notes.11:6: The earliest manuscripts end the verse here; later manuscripts add a parallel balancing clause stating that if it is by works, it is no longer grace, otherwise work is no longer work.
notes.11:17: The Greek links two successive genitives without a conjunction (of the root, of the richness of the olive tree), emphasizing that Gentile believers share in the nourishing richness of Israel's covenant root.
notes.11:31: Many early manuscripts include the second "now" before "be shown mercy," highlighting the present-age reality of Israel's reception of mercy; the dative phrase "through the mercy shown to you" is fronted before the purpose clause.
notes.12:1: Greek logiken latreian ('reasonable worship' or 'spiritual service') denotes worship offered with the whole rational self, not merely ritual formality.
notes.12:2: The Saints Greek Critical Text reads tou noos ('of the mind') without a possessive pronoun, and in v. 14 omits 'you' after 'those who persecute.'
notes.12:3: Paul weaves a fourfold Greek wordplay around phroneo ('think'): hyperphronein ('think too highly'), phronein ('think'), and sophronein ('be sober-minded').
notes.12:16: Greek tois tapeinois is ambiguous between neuter ('lowly things/tasks') and masculine ('lowly persons'); 'the lowly' preserves that breadth.
notes.12:20: Quoting Proverbs 25:21-22, the Greek shifts from second-person plural (vv. 1-19) to second-person singular here and in the imperatives of v. 21.
notes.13:1: The Greek reads "by God" (hypo theou) in both clauses, underscoring direct divine agency in ordaining civil authority.
notes.13:9: The critical Greek text cites four commandments from the Decalogue before summarizing the law with Leviticus 19:18; later manuscripts add "You shall not bear false witness."
notes.13:11: The critical Greek text reads "for you" (hymas) before shifting to "our salvation" (hemon), whereas later manuscripts harmonize the first pronoun to "for us."
notes.14:6: The Greek critical text omits the additional clause "and the one who does not observe the day does not observe it to the Lord," which appears in later manuscripts.
notes.14:10: The Greek critical text reads "the judgment seat of God" rather than "the judgment seat of Christ," a later variant likely harmonized with 2 Corinthians 5:10.
notes.14:20: The Greek phrase rendered "causes stumbling by his eating" (literally "eats through stumbling") is debated and may mean either causing a fellow believer to stumble or eating against one's own troubled conscience.
notes.14:21: The Greek text here retains the fuller threefold sequence "stumbles, or is ensnared, or becomes weak," whereas some manuscripts contain only "stumbles."
notes.15:7: The Greek critical text reads "received you" rather than "received us," sharpening Paul's direct appeal to the Roman congregations.
notes.15:19: The Greek text reads "the Spirit of God," where ancient manuscripts vary among "the Spirit of God," "the Holy Spirit," and simply "the Spirit."
notes.15:24: The Greek critical text omits "I will come to you" after "Spain," leaving an abrupt pause before Paul resumes his thought in verse 25.
notes.15:29: The Greek critical text reads "the blessing of Christ" without the additional words "of the gospel" found in later manuscripts.
notes.16:1: Greek diakonos can denote either a general servant or minister or an official deacon or deaconess of the church.
notes.16:7: The Greek phrase episemoi en tois apostolois is debated and may mean either 'distinguished among the apostles' (counting Andronicus and Junia within the broader circle of apostles) or 'well known to the apostles.' The Greek name Iounian is standardly taken as the feminine name Junia.
notes.16:24: This benediction is enclosed in double brackets because it is omitted by the earliest manuscripts, though it appears in many later witnesses.
notes.16:27: The closing doxology (verses twenty-five through twenty-seven) exhibits a slight grammatical break at 'to whom,' referring back to God; in ancient manuscripts the doxology also appears after 14:23 or 15:33 in some witnesses.
